thesis: DELL's 60-day gain (396.34 -> 534.28, now 543.51 and a fresh all-time high) is anchored in a single, specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed event: the Q2 FY2027 earnings report on September 1, 2026, which posted a record $47.0B in revenue (+58% YoY, beat), non-GAAP EPS of $7.04 (+203% YoY, beat consensus $4.87 by $2.17), $60.9B of AI-server orders booked in the quarter, a record $95B AI-server backlog, traditional server/networking revenue up 122% to $10.5B, and a $25B raise to full-year revenue guidance (new midpoint ~$192B, AI-server revenue guide ~$74B). This is a completed, disclosed print, not a rumor, technical pattern, or macro-wide move. The strongest counter-evidence is margin compression on the AI-server business: Dell's gross margin has fallen to roughly 18.1% (from 20%+ historically) because Nvidia GPU economics leave Dell thin assembly-level margins, a well-documented concern that drove a prior 7% one-day drop after the Feb 2025 report and was again a major analyst focus on the Sept 1 call. This doesn't change the bullish read, however, because it is not new information -- it was disclosed and discussed on the same earnings call that drove the rally, and the stock has continued climbing to fresh all-time highs through Sept 11-15 despite the market already knowing about it, indicating the market is currently weighting the revenue/backlog growth and guidance raise above the margin dilution. The required litigation check found two active but not-yet-scheduled matters, neither disqualifying under the required bar: an XTX Markets Finland unit suit (~$70M) over server pricing tied to data-center contracts, and an ERISA class action (filed Jan 28, 2026, W.D. Tex., alleging $318M in 401(k) mismanagement losses) that remains at the complaint stage -- neither has a scheduled ruling, hearing, or trial date within the next ~90 days. The required governance check found no confirmed accounting restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea involving a current or former Dell executive in the last three years; PwC was routinely reappointed as auditor in June 2024, and CFO Yvonne McGill's September 2025 resignation was explicitly stated as not due to any disagreement with the company (also outside the 3-year and 90-day windows regardless). No dilutive equity or convertible raise was found in the last 90 days -- the $3B senior notes offering completed June 16, 2026 is straight debt, and Silver Lake's Class B-to-C conversions are a pre-existing conversion right, not new capital raised. No insolvency or liquidity concern exists given the record cash generation, and no leadership turnover tied to operational or execution problems occurred in the last 90 days. Dell's next earnings report (Q3 FY2027) is not expected until around November 24, 2026, well beyond this position's next likely review, so no unresolved binary catalyst threatens to reverse the read in the near term.
invalidation: Thesis weakens or flips if: the November 24, 2026 Q3 FY2027 report misses the raised guidance or shows AI-server order momentum/backlog decelerating; gross margin erosion accelerates beyond what management has already characterized, signaling a structural (not just mix-driven) profitability problem; the XTX Markets or ERISA litigation acquires a near-term scheduled hearing/ruling with adverse exposure; or evidence emerges of a Dell-specific accounting, auditor, or executive-conduct issue, or a dilutive equity/convertible raise.

thesis: BWIN's trigger today (near a fresh 52-week high, a 5.98x volume spike, and a 17.4% 60-day gain) is a specific, confirmed, company-disclosed event: on September 14, 2026 Baldwin's board unanimously approved, on recommendation of an independent special committee, a definitive go-private merger agreement in which an entity formed by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management (Michael Dell's family office) will acquire the company for $32.50/share in cash (~$7.7B enterprise value, an ~88% premium to the unaffected mid-June price), with close targeted for Q1 2027. The live price (~$32.48) sits essentially at the deal price, which is itself the clearest evidence available that the market already prices high odds of completion -- a spread this tight (~0.06%) would not persist if there were material doubt the deal closes. That said, this doesn't fully resolve the risk: the deal still needs multi-state insurance-regulatory approval and a shareholder vote (no vote date has been announced yet) before the Q1 2027 close, and a chunk of the 60-day run predates the confirmed agreement -- speculative buyout chatter from analysts (BMO, KBW) in late June already moved the stock before Sept 14's signed contract, so part of this move traces to rumor/analyst opinion rather than a confirmed event, which is why this stays at medium rather than high. The required litigation check found only boilerplate post-announcement 'fairness' investigations from plaintiff firms (Brodsky & Smith, Halper Sadeh, Ademi) with no scheduled hearing, trial date, or ruling -- color only, not a qualifying flag. The required governance check found no confirmed accounting restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea in the last three years; PwC remains auditor. An October 2024 Blue Orca short-seller report alleging 'financial engineering' prompted law-firm investigations but remains an unresolved allegation, not a confirmed event, so it does not meet the governance_history bar. No dilutive raise applies -- the deal is cash-funded by the acquirers, not the company. No insolvency concern exists ($184.5M cash plus $259.4M available borrowing capacity alongside record EBITDA at 6/30/26). The only leadership changes in the window are routine, planned successions (a UCTS segment CEO transition effective 1/1/2027, and an interim Chief Accounting Officer appointment tied to maternity leave), not distress-driven, so no leadership_turnover flag applies.
invalidation: Thesis weakens or flips if: the merger agreement is terminated, renegotiated at a lower price, or a financing/regulatory condition is not met; a competing bidder emerges without a corresponding price bump (reducing certainty rather than adding value); litigation produces a scheduled hearing with a real chance of blocking or delaying the deal; or the special committee/board process is credibly challenged as unfair to shareholders in a way that could unwind the agreed price.

thesis: FPS's signal today reflects two distinct, both company-disclosed events layered on top of each other. The 60-day decline (39.79 -> 28.64) traces to a confirmed dilution event, not deteriorating fundamentals: sponsor Neos Partners LP (which assembled Forgent from four legacy equipment makers and took it public in Feb 2026) has been monetizing its stake since the IPO lock-up expired Aug 4, 2026, including an upsized secondary offering of roughly 43.65M shares priced at $49.00. The stock fell as much as 35% over 30 days and 16-17% in a single week in August on this sponsor-selling pressure. Today's sharp reversal (an 11% premarket pop, elevated volume) is a separate, confirmed catalyst: a Q4 FY2026 earnings beat reported this morning -- revenue $462M (+94% YoY) versus ~$425-430M expected, bookings $1.5B (+375%), backlog $3.0B (+256% YoY, book-to-bill 3.3x), Adj. EBITDA $113M (+163%), plus a raised FY2026 revenue guide of $1.35-1.39B and a new FY2027 guide of $2.4-2.6B revenue / $575-625M Adj. EBITDA. That is a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed operating result -- the dominant driver of today's price action -- not a rumor or macro move. The strongest counter-evidence is that the earnings beat does not resolve the dilution overhang: Neos Partners still holds a large post-IPO stake and has shown a repeated pattern of selling since the lock-up expired, so further sponsor-driven share supply remains a live, un-dismissed risk even against strong operating results -- this ongoing behavioral pattern (rather than a one-time resolved event) is the primary reason conviction is capped well below high. The required litigation check found an active suit, Gougerchian v. Neos Partners LP, in LA County Superior Court (alleging the plaintiff was squeezed out of a 50% stake in a predecessor company's 2023 sale to Neos, with an initial dismissal attempt rejected by the court in Nov 2025); no hearing, trial date, or ruling was found scheduled within the next ~90 days, so it stays color-only rather than a qualifying flag. The required governance check found no confirmed accounting restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or executive indictment/plea -- the company was only founded in 2025/IPO'd in Feb 2026, so the 3-year lookback finds essentially nothing to report; BDO USA remains auditor with no dismissal reported. On dilution/insolvency/leadership: the Aug 4, 2026 lock-up expiry and upsized secondary offering are squarely inside the 90-day window and are exactly the kind of disclosed share-offering event the dilution_risk flag exists for, so it is flagged. No insolvency or going-concern language was found -- the company just posted strong EBITDA and raised guidance. A new CFO (Ryan Fiedler, ex-Caterpillar Resource Industries) was appointed, but available reporting could not confirm whether this replaced a departed CFO tied to any problem or the exact date, so it is not treated as a confirmed leadership_turnover flag, just a note for future monitoring.
invalidation: Thesis weakens or flips if: Neos Partners begins another large secondary sale or the lock-up-driven selling pattern resumes and outweighs the earnings-driven bounce; the FY2027 guidance ($2.4-2.6B revenue) is walked back or the 3.3x book-to-bill fails to convert to delivered revenue; the Gougerchian litigation acquires a near-term scheduled hearing with real exposure; or the new CFO appointment turns out to reflect an unreported departure tied to operational problems.
sources: Yahoo Finance / Stone LLP (Gougerchian v. Neos Partners litigation): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/forgent-power-solutions-parent-neos-204600892.html

thesis: SRRK's volume-spike signal today is downstream of a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed event: the FDA approved ISEMBYLD (apitegromab-mstn) on September 11, 2026 -- the first muscle-targeted treatment for spinal muscular atrophy -- ahead of its September 30 PDUFA date, a completed regulatory approval, not a rumor or pending catalyst. The stock initially jumped ~12-15% after-hours on the news, but has since pulled back to ~$50 (from a post-approval peak above $61) as investors digested the announced net pricing (~$310K/year) and Barclays downgraded the stock to Equalweight from Overweight on valuation grounds (even while raising its price target to $58), framing further upside as now dependent on commercial-launch execution rather than approval risk. This pullback is best read as a valuation reset / 'sell the news' dynamic following a resolved binary rather than a deteriorating fundamental picture -- multiple other analysts (Citi, Truist, Raymond James) raised targets post-approval and consensus remains Strong Buy -- but the framing of the current dip as sentiment/valuation-driven, on top of a real dilution flag below, is why this stays at low rather than higher conviction. The required litigation check found only an open-ended Kuehn Law fiduciary-duty investigation (announced ~July 2026) with no filed suit or scheduled hearing/ruling date -- color only. The required governance check found no confirmed accounting restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea in the last three years; the April 2025 CEO/CFO transition (Backstrom out, Hallal/Sinha in) was outside the window and not disclosed as a for-cause event. On dilution/insolvency/leadership: Scholar Rock filed a prospectus supplement on August 6, 2026 expanding its at-the-market equity program by $200M with Jefferies (after already raising ~$257.7M net under the prior ATM), squarely inside the 90-day window -- a clear, confirmed dilution_risk flag for a clinical-stage biotech now transitioning into commercial launch. No going-concern language applies; the company ended Q2 2026 with $492M in cash/investments and guided runway into 2027. No leadership turnover occurred within the 90-day window.
invalidation: Thesis weakens or flips if: commercial launch/payer-coverage data for ISEMBYLD disappoints relative to the ~$310K pricing; Scholar Rock draws heavily on the expanded ATM program in a way that materially increases share count; the Kuehn Law investigation converts into a filed suit with a scheduled near-term hearing; or pipeline readouts (OPAL Phase 2, FSHD Phase 2, SRK-439 Phase 1) disappoint.

thesis: SPCX's 60-day gain (123.99 -> 148.15) does not trace to one dominant, confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst -- it reads as a technical/sentiment rebound layered on a forward-looking narrative. The stock bottomed at $104.83 on Aug 3 around the first big insider lock-up unlock (~911.5M shares, ~20% of eligible insider stock) on Aug 6; the Aug 4 Q2 earnings beat (revenue +92% YoY to $7.8B) was itself undercut after-hours by a capex shock ($18.37B in the quarter, $15.83B AI-related), and the subsequent recovery is attributed by reporting to a mix of broad AI/market strength, technical reclaiming of moving averages, anticipation of the first orbital Starship test, a $100B ARR target for year-end 2026, and new Starlink mobile-carrier deals -- multiple contributing factors without one clearly resolved as dominant, and explicitly technical framing ('reclaiming moving averages') for part of the move. The strongest counter-evidence is the cash-burn profile: Q2 burn was roughly $16B, Goldman projects ~$350B of cumulative burn through 2030, S&P doesn't see positive free cash flow until 2029, and the company's own $25B debut bond trades at junk-like secondary spreads despite an investment-grade rating -- credit investors are notably more skeptical than the equity market's rally would suggest, and this is not resolved, only noted. On top of the diffuse catalyst picture and unresolved cash-burn concern, there is a genuine near-term binary that could swing the stock either way within this position's likely review window: Starship Flight Test 14, the company's first orbital attempt, is now targeted for on/around September 22, 2026 -- a real risk of reversal, not a remote one. The required litigation check found no matter with a scheduled ruling, hearing, or trial date within 90 days (the Boca Chica beach-access case was already resolved in SpaceX's favor in June 2026; a land-swap suit had an Aug 25 hearing with no ruling reported; a property-damage suit has no hearing scheduled). The required governance check found no confirmed restatement, auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea; an advocacy group's May 2026 SEC letter about related-party accounting remains an unresolved request for scrutiny, not a confirmed governance event. On dilution/insolvency/leadership: further large lock-up tranches continue on a set schedule through Nov/Dec 2026 (pre-existing insider unlocks, not a new capital raise, so this does not meet the dilution_risk bar), no going-concern language was found despite the elevated burn, and xAI-subsidiary CFO turnover (two departures in 2026) is at a subsidiary rather than the SpaceX/SPCX issuer itself and was not tied to a disclosed operational failure. Given the mixed/diffuse catalyst picture, the unresolved cash-burn overhang, and a live binary event (Starship Flight 14) sitting inside the next review window that could move the stock sharply in either direction, this is better treated as avoid than as a new long entry for a small account right now.
invalidation: Would reconsider toward long if: Starship Flight 14 succeeds cleanly and the stock holds its gains through the following lock-up tranches without a renewed slide; a hyperscaler-scale AI-computing revenue contract actually starts billing (per the Dec 1 start date referenced in company commentary) and cash burn visibly improves; or credit-market skepticism (bond spreads) narrows toward what the equity rally implies.

thesis: This is a held position; today's review reassesses whether yesterday's long thesis still holds. Marvell fell roughly 6-7% intraday on September 14 alongside Broadcom and Nvidia on sentiment tied to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's public call to slow frontier AI development -- a macro/sector-wide move, not company-specific bad news. As of today (Sept 15) the stock is essentially flat versus yesterday's close (~$218.82 -> ~$221.75), consistent with the drop stabilizing rather than deepening. No hyperscaler has confirmed cutting AI capex; to the contrary, combined 2026 capex guidance from Google/Amazon/Microsoft/Meta remains near record levels (~$725B, up ~77% YoY), and Piper Sandler initiated coverage in early September at Overweight / $270. The underlying long thesis -- the August 19, 2026 disclosed Google/Alphabet TPU-ecosystem warrant (up to ~58.97M shares tied to up to $120B of cumulative purchases through FY2033) and the August 27, 2026 Q2 FY2027 earnings beat with raised FY2027/FY2028 guidance -- remains intact and undisturbed: no news surfaced that the warrant's milestones were missed or renegotiated, or that any design win was lost. The strongest counter-evidence is that the AI-pacing rhetoric could recur and pressure the stock again even without hard data behind it, and this is not fully resolved (no hyperscaler has explicitly confirmed or denied a spending slowdown) -- it remains a live sentiment risk rather than a dismissed one, which is why this stays at medium. The required litigation check found no active matter naming Marvell (or an exec) with a scheduled ruling, hearing, or trial date in the next ~90 days -- the only litigation surfaced (a POET Technologies securities class action tied to Marvell's order cancellations) names POET, not Marvell, as defendant. The required governance check found no confirmed restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea in the last three years (the 2006-08 stock-option backdating matter and 2019 SEC revenue-recognition settlement are both outside the window); the June 2026 CFO transition (Meintjes -> Dan Durn) reads as routine, with the prior CFO retained in an advisory role and the incoming CFO carrying a deep semiconductor background. No new dilution, insolvency, or leadership-turnover flag applies in the last 90 days -- the Google warrant itself (already known since Aug 19) is a customer purchase-incentive instrument, not a capital-raising equity/convertible/ATM offering, so it is not treated as dilution_risk.
invalidation: Flip to exit_existing if: hyperscaler AI capex (especially Google's TPU/custom-silicon purchasing) is concretely cut back or the Google warrant's purchasing milestones are missed or renegotiated; the AI-pacing sentiment translates into an actual announced capex reduction by a major customer rather than remaining rhetorical; Q3 FY2027 results (expected around Nov 26, 2026) miss guidance or show data-center deceleration; or a new governance red flag or dilutive raise is disclosed.

thesis: This is a held position; today's review reassesses whether the long thesis still holds. The required litigation check found an active securities class action (N.D. Cal., consolidated, alleging overstated property holdings and an undisclosed failed China-subsidiary listing) currently in a second round of dismissal-motion briefing, with no specific ruling or hearing date confirmed within the next ~90 days -- color only, not a qualifying flag. The required governance check found no confirmed accounting restatement, for-cause auditor dismissal, or indictment/plea involving a current or former AXT executive in the last three years. On dilution/insolvency/leadership: AXT priced an underwritten public offering (8,560,311 shares plus a 1,284,046-share over-allotment at $64.25, ~$632.5M combined) on April 21, 2026 to fund InP capacity expansion -- material and dilutive, but at ~147 days before today it falls just outside the ~90-day dilution_risk window, so it is not flagged, though it remains the dominant capital-structure event of the year and materially increased float. No going-concern language was found (the company is well-capitalized post-raise and profitable), and no leadership turnover tied to operational or execution problems occurred in the last 90 days -- only routine board-committee changes, with CEO Morris Young and CFO Gary Fischer unchanged.
invalidation: Flip to exit_existing if: short interest unwinds sharply and the stock gives back the momentum-driven portion of the rally without a corresponding fundamental deterioration explanation; the InP demand/backlog story is contradicted by a weak print at the next earnings report (~Oct 29, 2026); the securities litigation acquires a near-term scheduled ruling with adverse exposure; or another large dilutive raise is announced.
